items.stem: You add `public int Grade { get; set; }` to a POCO. It compiles and runs, but some Grade changes never sync to the destination. What rule did you break?

options.text: Synnduit POCO properties must be nullable; a bare non-nullable int breaks change detection
POCOs cannot have integer properties at all

items.explanation: Synnduit requires properties to be nullable. A non-nullable int prevents the engine from reliably detecting changes, so updates are silently missed.

misconceptions.b: The type doesn't need to become a string — it needs to become nullable (int?) or use a nullable proxy.
misconceptions.d: Integers are fine; they just need to be nullable (int?).

items.stem: Why does Synnduit require POCO properties to be nullable?

options.text: So the engine can represent 'no value' and tell it apart from a real default (0, false), which change detection depends on
Because EF cannot map non-nullable types
To make every field optional in the UI

items.explanation: The nullable distinction lets the engine separate 'absent' from a legitimate default value, which is what reliable change detection needs.

misconceptions.c: EF maps non-nullable types fine; this is a Synnduit change-detection requirement, not an EF limitation.

items.stem: You need a property to stay non-nullable (`int EnrollmentStatus`) for the destination, but satisfy Synnduit's nullable rule. What is the correct pattern?

options.text: Mark it [Required] and hope for the best
Add a [NotMapped] nullable proxy property and wire it via [EntityProperty(NullableProxyProperty = nameof(...))]

items.explanation: The nullable-proxy pattern keeps the non-nullable property but routes the engine through a [NotMapped] nullable proxy linked by the NullableProxyProperty annotation.

misconceptions.d: Removing [EntityProperty] would stop tracking the field entirely — the opposite of what you want.

items.stem: When using the nullable-proxy pattern, where does the feed's Map method assign the incoming source value?

options.text: To the nullable proxy property; Synnduit moves it to the non-nullable one internally via the annotation
It doesn't — the engine reads the database column directly

items.explanation: You assign to the nullable proxy (e.g. c.NullableEnrollmentStatus = reader.GetInt32(11)); the engine propagates it to the non-nullable property through the NullableProxyProperty link.

items.stem: Why is the non-nullable-property bug especially dangerous, and what do you see in the console after applying the fix and re-running in test?
rubric: Dangerous because it is silent: no compile error and no exception — it appears to work, but some changes are never picked up
After the fix, re-running shows the engine reconciling the affected records, with NoChangesMerged entries counted in the console as it corrects them
items.sampleAnswer: It's dangerous because nothing fails loudly — the code compiles and runs, so you assume it works, while certain field changes silently never sync. After switching to nullable (or the proxy pattern) and re-running in test, the console shows the correction progressing, with NoChangesMerged entries as it reconciles the previously-missed records.
